To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

receptor-mediated internalization is an important clearance mechanism for a therapeutic antibody against EGFR and that the pharmacokinetic effect of this mechanism may vary between tumor models with different levels of EGFR overexpression.
the pharmacokinetics of the novel therapeutic antibody 2F8 is nonlinear and that the nonlinear pharmacokinetics is due to receptor-mediated antibody internalisation and degradation.

receptor-mediated antibody clearance is saturable and may significantly affect pharmacokinetics, especially at low antibody doses, and that the mechanism of action may be affected by receptor internalization, which reduces local antibody concentrations in tumor tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the effect of receptor dynamics on the pharmacokinetic behavior of a novel mAb.
the effect of target dynamics on antibody clearance and tissue distribution.
the effect of target dynamics on the pharmacokinetic profile of a novel therapeutic monoclonal anti-epidermal growth factor antibody.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pharmacokinetics of 2F 8 is affected by the receptor-mediated internalization and degradation of 2F.

the receptor mediated antibody internalization and clearance significantly affects the PK, particularly at low doses and that EGFR saturation in the normal tissues does not always predict the saturation in tumor tissues.
receptor-mediated clearance of a therapeutic antibody can significantly affect its pharmacokinetic profile and the local concentration in tumor tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
receptor-mediated antibody clearance can affect the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy of therapeutic antibodies.
receptor-mediated clearance of 2F81 is an important factor to consider for the development of therapeutic antibodies against EGFR.
receptor-mediated antibody clearance is an important pharmacokinetic determinant of the dose-effect relationship of therapeutic antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pharmacokinetics of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies can be affected by the pharmacodynamics of the drug, i.e., the mechanism of action of the antibody.
receptor-mediated antibody internalisation and degradation is an important mechanism for the clearance of therapeutic antibodies.
antibody internalization and clearance is not only an issue for the development of therapeutic mAb but also for the development of imaging agents.
